categories.name: Ransomware
actions: Immediately disconnect the affected device from the network (unplug Ethernet / turn off Wi-Fi).
Do NOT pay the ransom and do NOT restart the device.
Do not attempt to delete or rename the encrypted files.
Report to the security/IT team immediately as a Critical incident.
Preserve the ransom note as evidence for the security team.

categories.name: Phishing
actions: Do not click any links or download attachments in the email.
Do not reply with any personal or financial information.
Report the email to IT/security using the 'report phishing' option.
If you already clicked a link or entered credentials, change that password immediately and notify IT.
Delete the email after reporting it.

categories.name: Unauthorized Access
keywords: login alert i did not request
actions: Change your password immediately from a trusted, uncompromised device.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) if not already active.
Review recent account activity and revoke sessions/devices you don't recognize.
Notify the security team so they can check for further compromise.
Check for unauthorized changes to account recovery details (email/phone).

categories.name: Malware / Virus
actions: Disconnect the device from the network to prevent spread.
Do not open any unfamiliar files or programs.
Run a full antivirus/anti-malware scan if the device is still safe to use.
Report the incident to IT/security with details of what you observed.
Avoid using the device for sensitive logins (banking, email) until it is cleared.

categories.name: Data Leak / Exposure
keywords: sent sensitive data to wrong person
actions: Immediately revoke access/sharing on the exposed file or resource if possible.
Do not attempt to quietly delete the shared item without informing security — an audit trail is needed.
Report to the security/compliance team immediately as a Critical incident.
Identify exactly what data was exposed and to whom.
Prepare for possible breach-notification obligations depending on data sensitivity.

categories.name: Lost / Stolen Device
actions: Report the loss/theft to IT/security immediately.
Remotely lock or wipe the device if management tools are available.
Change passwords for all accounts that were logged in on the device.
File a report with local authorities if it was stolen.
Revoke any active sessions tied to that device.

categories.name: Payment / UPI Safety
actions: Do not share your OTP, UPI PIN, card PIN, CVV, or screen with anyone; receiving money never requires a PIN.
Check the transaction in the official payment/bank app and save the transaction ID, time, amount, and screenshots.
For an unauthorized transaction, immediately contact your bank or payment provider through its official app or number and request that the account/card be secured.
Change the payment-app password/PIN from a trusted device and remove unknown devices or linked accounts.
Report suspected fraud promptly to your local cybercrime or financial-fraud reporting service.

categories.name: Password / Account Help
actions: Use only the service's official app or website and its built-in password-reset or account-recovery page.
Create a new, unique passphrase; do not reuse a password from email, banking, or another important account.
Turn on two-factor authentication (prefer an authenticator app where available) and store backup codes safely.
Review recovery email, phone number, logged-in devices, and recent activity; remove anything you do not recognize.
Never give a password, recovery code, OTP, or verification link to a person claiming to be support.

categories.name: Account Privacy / Security
actions: Open the account's Privacy and Security settings using the official app or website.
Use a unique password and enable two-factor authentication.
Limit profile visibility, location sharing, and third-party app permissions to only what you need.
Remove unfamiliar connected apps, browser extensions, devices, and active sessions.
Keep your recovery email and phone number current and protected.

categories.name: Device Performance / Basic Safety
actions: Restart the device, install trusted system updates, and check storage space and unnecessary startup apps.
Run a full scan with your installed antivirus or the device's built-in security tool; do not install random cleaner apps.
If the slowness started after a suspicious download, pop-up, or unknown app, disconnect from the internet and seek IT/security help.

categories.name: Cybersecurity Basics
actions: Cybersecurity means protecting devices, accounts, networks, and data from unauthorized access, scams, and damage.
Hacking is attempting to access or affect a system without permission; never attempt it on accounts, devices, or networks you do not own or have written permission to test.
Use unique passwords, multi-factor authentication, software updates, backups, and caution with links or downloads as your core protection.
If this relates to a real compromise, describe what happened (account, device, message, payment, or data) so it can be triaged more precisely.

default.name: Unclassified
actions: This description didn't clearly match a known incident pattern.
Try describing it with more specific detail (e.g. what happened, what device/account was involved).
If you believe this is a genuine security concern, report it to your IT/security team directly.
